deep.reconstruction:
The page is struck through with a large inverted V. It continues the previous page, which set up lifting-property (RLP) criteria. In that setup, a functor with the RLP against ∅→e and against maps of the form ∂×S^n(N)→I×S^n(N) (S^n probably an iterated subdivision, N in a 'fundamental' family of test categories) has W∞-aspherical fibres. The RLP against 'cones' on these maps gives W∞-properness, resp. W∞-smoothness.

Here W∞ is the basic localizer of weak equivalences of nerves; 'propre' and 'lisse' are the homotopical analogues of proper and smooth base change used in Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs.

This page draws a consequence. Ch(C) is a 'category of paths' (chemins) in a small category C. It comes with p = (s,b): Ch(C) → C×C, where s and b are source and end ('but').

(1) The argument shows that p has homotopical properties 'of fibration type'. Yet in the categorical sense p has none of them: it is neither a Grothendieck fibration nor a cofibration. Neither are the composites s∘p and b∘p : Ch(C) → C. And p is neither a 'cat. propre' nor a 'cat. lisse' map in the purely categorical sense.

(2) He asks whether s∘p and b∘p are at least one or the other. He then remarks that what really matters to him are the properties of p itself.

(3) Conjecture: p should be a W∞-fibration (parenthetically, a 'cohomological fibration'), 'to be checked', apparently after some letter ('L. à B.', perhaps a letter to R. Brown or to Breen).

Final question: do the W∞-fibrations, together with the corresponding cofibrations, form a Quillen (closed model) structure on Cat?

Purpose: build a path-space object for categories as models of homotopy types. The fibre of p over (x,y) should model the space of paths from x to y. The page then asks whether this fits into a model structure on Cat whose weak equivalences are W∞.
errors: No outright error can be detected. The claim that p is a W∞-fibration is explicitly left as a conjecture.

Gap: 'W∞-fibration' is not defined on this page. If it means a Thomason fibration (RLP against Ex²Sd²-type trivial cofibrations), it is unlikely that path categories of an arbitrary C give such fibrations, since Thomason-fibrant objects are very restricted. If it means a 'cohomological' or quasi-fibration in the sense that strict fibres compute homotopy fibres (Quillen Theorem B type), the conjecture is much more plausible. The page does not disambiguate.

ideas.what: Path category Ch(C) with endpoint map p:Ch(C)→C×C as a path-space object for small categories, homotopically a fibration but not categorically one
ideas.modern_name: path object / homotopy fibration (quasi-fibration) of categories; Theorem B-type fibres
ideas.where_published: Similar path/cylinder considerations occur in Pursuing Stacks (1983); exact Ch(C) construction unsure

ideas.what: Contrast between categorical fibration/cofibration/proper/smooth and their W∞-homotopical analogues
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks, Les Dérivateurs); Maltsiniotis; Cisinski

ideas.what: Question whether W∞-fibrations and the corresponding cofibrations give a Quillen model structure on Cat
ideas.modern_name: Thomason model structure on Cat; Cisinski's model structures for basic localizers
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses model structures on Cat

missed.claim: Conjecture that the endpoint functor of the path category, Ch(C)→C×C, is a W∞-('cohomological') fibration, even though it is not a categorical (co)fibration and not categorically proper or smooth.
missed.quote: Il semblerait que p soit une W∞-fibration. ("fibrations cohomologiques") C'est une chose à vérifier.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a functorial path object in Cat whose strict fibres model path spaces. That would be useful for homotopy-type theoretic or Theorem B style computations. It is already largely covered by Quillen's Theorem B, Thomason's work and Cisinski's work, so it is likely of minor novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: The model-structure question was answered by Thomason (1980) and generalized to arbitrary basic localizers by Cisinski. The path-category fibration conjecture is a natural, unfinished side remark of modest interest.
